connections.implementation: New self-hosted canonical profile reusing the AWS S3 security runtime with forced path-style addressing and a connection-scoped custom X.509 CA transport.
connections.auth: S3-compatible access key ID and secret key, with optional session token and custom CA, stored as an encrypted custom credential.
scopes: Configured endpoint, bucket, and optional object-key prefix allowlist; no write scope is exposed.
connections.evidence: Contract tests prove path-style request construction, configured bucket/prefix discovery, required bucket binding, endpoint pinning, stat-before-download automatic version/ETag pinning and race rejection, invalid-CA rejection, bounded CA-agent caching, shared bounded-read controls, and a 30-second validation timeout across bucket fallback.
limitations: Private endpoints require OOMOL_CONNECT_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK and remain subject to metadata, loopback, link-local, redirect, and DNS guards.
A custom PEM CA is supported on Node deployments and validated before use; Cloudflare cannot reach private MinIO networks.
MinIO evidence does not promote AWS S3 or other vendors to verified.
connections.revocation: Connection deletion and credential replacement advance the revision, invalidating existing leases and discovered resources on the next invocation; server-side key rotation requires a controlled MinIO deployment.
connections.externalBlocker: No controlled TLS/private-CA MinIO deployment was available for a full credential rotation and revocation lifecycle.

connections.implementation: New canonical provider using Qiniu V2 authorization against native RSF POST list and RS stat APIs; private object downloads use a five-minute token against the configured bucket domain and never return that token to callers.
connections.auth: Qiniu access key ID and secret key plus an HTTPS bucket download domain, stored as an encrypted custom credential.
scopes: Configured bucket and optional object-key prefix allowlist; no write scope is exposed.
connections.evidence: Contract tests cover an exact official-SDK V2 signature vector, RSF POST semantics, native endpoint construction, required bucket binding, configured-bucket discovery, prefix denial before egress, ETag race rejection, unsafe MIME and oversized-body rejection, redacted errors, and request timeouts.
connections.revocation: Connection deletion and credential replacement advance the revision, invalidating existing leases and discovered resources on the next invocation; cloud credential revocation requires a real account.
connections.externalBlocker: No Qiniu account/Kodo credential and bucket download domain were available for real service, credential rotation, and revocation evidence.

security.credentialOwnership: All credentials remain encrypted behind credential_ref and are resolved only inside the server runtime.
security.authorization: Discovery is connection-scoped; resource-bound reads exact-match the latest revision's ResourceRef and upstream access is checked again on every invocation. Successful leased Tencent Docs, WPS MCP, and Baidu Netdisk list/search actions append only bounded provider-returned identities after an atomic tenant/service/revision recheck; failed actions, guessed IDs, stale revisions, and cross-tenant observations add nothing. Expired OAuth credentials refresh before validation, discovery, lease issuance, and action execution; the atomic credential update advances the connection revision so pre-refresh leases fail closed.
security.leasePolicy: Office mutations, generic WPS tool calls, storage writes/deletes, and presigned URLs cannot enter Agent leases.
security.storage: Bucket and prefix are allowlisted, endpoint overrides are pinned to the configured origin, reads are streamed/bounded, unsafe MIME is rejected, and version/ETag preconditions are preserved. COS and OBS perform native HEAD-before-download, while MinIO and Qiniu perform stat-before-download, pinning the observed version/ETag and rejecting object replacement races.
security.ssrf: Public storage endpoints use public-only DNS validation. MinIO private networking requires the deployment-level opt-in and cannot reach cloud metadata or other always-blocked addresses.
